note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a NET 8(1); A06b NET 8(1); L05 NET 15(1)(a), 16(1)(e)): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships (with major exceptions); a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another (with exceptions). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. The Kingdom Act as consolidated today still asks five years' admission and principal residence immediately before the request (art. 8(1)(c)). Citizenship at birth is read from article 3 of the same consolidated Kingdom Act: a child is Dutch if the father or the mother is Dutch at the birth, or a Dutch parent died before it (art. 3(1)), wherever the child is born; birth in the Kingdom gives it only in the third generation (art. 3(3)). Foundlings (art. 3(2)) aren't held by the form, nor the loss later of a Dutch national living abroad for long (art. 15). Naturalisation costs €1,139 for one person (IND, read 30 October 2026); the applicant must have passed the civic integration exam, in Dutch at least at A2 and in knowledge of Dutch society; the IND has a legal decision period of 12 months, which it may extend by 1 year in total, so the longest held is 24 months.

sources.said: Person has been resident in the Netherlands for 5 years immediately before the application and there are no objections against indefinite residence in the country. ... Renunciation or automatic loss of citizenship of another country (with exceptions). ... Person voluntarily acquires citizenship of another country. Provision does not apply if person is born and resides in another country, or resided in another country for 5 years before majority, or is married to a citizen of another country (adults), or his/her parent is citizen of the Netherlands (minors), or acquired citizenship by birth in the Netherlands. No exception to main rule if Article 1 of 1963 Strasbourg Convention applies.
